The test image shows a soybean plant that remains green (stems and leaves) while all surrounding plants have fully senesced and turned brown/dry. This is a whole_plant symptom. The most obvious candidate is **Green_stem_disorder**, but let me also consider other possibilities like Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus (green stems after maturity).

Let me view reference images, one at a time, starting with my top candidates.
Very similar pattern - green plant with retained leaves among fully senesced brown plants. Let me check other candidates.
BPMV shows leaf mottling/puckering - not matching. Let me check more candidates.
SDS shows interveinal chlorosis/necrosis with leaflet drop - different from the test image. Let me check more.
SCN shows stunted/yellowing plants - different from the test image. Let me check more candidates.
Charcoal rot shows wilting/dying plants - not matching. Let me check more.
Phytophthora shows dying/wilting patches within a green field - opposite of the test image. Let me check two more.
This Green_stem_disorder stem reference is very similar to the test image - green stems with mature/dry pods while surrounding plants are fully senesced. One more view.

Brown Stem Rot shows interveinal necrosis on leaves - not matching.

The evidence is clear. The test image shows a soybean plant with green stems and retained green leaves standing among a field of fully senesced, dry, brown plants. This is the hallmark symptom of Green_stem_disorder: "All or part of the soybean plant remains green while the rest of the plant or neighboring plants mature and senesce." Both Green_stem_disorder reference images (whole_plant and stem) showed the same pattern as the test image.
